title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
technique: workflow-aware KV prefix-cache eviction (steps-to-execution from Agent Step Graph) plus overlapped CPU-to-GPU KV prefetching

optimized_metrics.evidence: Together, these optimizations significantly improve cache efficiency and reduce latency in executing agentic workflows.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Latency is averaged over all runs

headline_claim.text: Compared to SGLang with hierarchical radix cache, KVFlow achieves up to 1.83× speedup for single workflows with large prompts, and up to 2.19× speedup for scenarios with many concurrent workflows.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 5 (single 10-agent workflow, batch=1, speedup over SGLang), Fig 6 (concurrent workflows), Fig 8 (PEER workflows)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We begin by evaluating the latency of executing a single agentic workflow under batch size = 1. This single-request latency reflects interactive usage scenarios where workflows are triggered individually by a user
metric_definitions.notes: Workflow-level latency = time to execute the 10 sequential agent LLM calls; averaged over ten runs. No formal TTFT/TPOT definition. Results are plotted as speedup (ratio of latency) over SGLang.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Therefore, our evaluation focuses exclusively on system performance metrics like the latency.
metric_definitions.notes: In §4.2 'performance' and 'speedup' are used without explicit definition (apparently latency/completion-time ratio); no throughput or percentile reported.

load_regime: batch=1 single workflow; fixed concurrency of 8-64 simultaneous independent workflows chosen so prefix caches still fit; PEER-style synthetic workflows
tradeoff_acknowledged: If concurrency is too high, all memory is consumed by active requests and the method is out of scope; HiCache can fall to 0.57x of SGLang under high concurrency (baseline, not KVFlow).
workloads: synthetic sequential 10-agent workflow with controlled fixed/dynamic/output lengths; PEER Financial QA 4-agent workflows
extractor_notes: Metric is mean workflow-level latency only; no tail, TTFT, TPOT or throughput. Evaluation explicitly says accuracy is unaffected so only latency is measured. Program-level (workflow) latency, not request-level.
load_class_quote: evaluating the latency of executing a single agentic workflow under batch size = 1 ... evaluate system performance under high concurrency by simultaneously launching multiple [§4.1 single workflow bs=1; §4.2 fixed concurrency of simultaneously launched workflows; no arrival process]
